findings.title: Null check validates grantType twice instead of rawTokenId
findings.body: The constructor uses Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed") for the fourth argument, so rawTokenId is never checked. When such a context is encoded, encodeTokenId concatenates null as 'null', which can produce malformed or non-unique token IDs. The intended invariant is that rawTokenId is non-null; the check should use rawTokenId.

findings.title: isAccessTokenId checks wrong substring with inverted condition
findings.body: The grant-type shortcut is at prefix positions 4-5 (e.g. onrtac -> ac), but substring(3, 5) extracts positions 3-4 (the token type), and the method returns false when those characters equal the expected grant shortcut. It never validates the actual grant type, and for refresh-token flows the token type shortcut rt equals the grant shortcut rt, so expectRefresh(...) will always fail for regular tokens. Use items[0].substring(4, 6) and return true on equality (or otherwise verify the correct segment).

findings.title: New abstract interface method breaks existing custom grant type providers
findings.body: getShortcut() is added as an abstract method to the public OAuth2GrantTypeFactory SPI. Existing compiled third-party grant type provider factories will fail with AbstractMethodError when loaded, and source code will no longer compile. Since this is a public Keycloak SPI, this is a binary/source compatibility break. Consider providing a default implementation (e.g. returning a neutral shortcut) or otherwise versioning the SPI.

findings.title: Removing public Context copy constructor breaks API consumers
findings.body: OAuth2GrantType.Context(Context context) was a public constructor on a public nested class in a SPI package and has been removed. Any existing custom grant implementation that clones the context will fail to compile or run. If the constructor is no longer wanted, it should be deprecated before removal or the new grantType field must be made available elsewhere; as-is this is an API contract break.
